clue.text: As secret ring I organised could be

definitions.text: As secret ring I organised could be

indicators.note: organised says the letters before it are put into a new arrangement

parts.note: a ring is round, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone muses that a secret ring they set up might count as an exclusive inner circle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' rearranges SECRET plus O (ring) and I. Read as a whole, the clue also describes the answer: a secret circle set up in private would be known only to a select few.
explanation.definitionFit: Something understood only by a select inner circle is hidden from outsiders, as a secret ring would be.

clue.text: Southern writer and athlete

parts.note: a printer is a machine that writes out text

explanation.surface: A clue listing two people: a writer from the South, and a sportsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writer' suggests an author, but here it is a machine that puts words on paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner who races over short distances is a particular kind of athlete.

clue.text: What might produce raging torrents and mud around Holyhead?

definitions.text: What might produce raging torrents and mud around Holyhead?

indicators.note: raging describes wild, disordered motion, so the words beside it are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the head (first letter) of Holy is H

explanation.surface: A question about what might cause floods and mud around Holyhead, a port town in north Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raging' rearranges TORRENTS, MUD and H, the head of 'Holy' in 'Holyhead'. The whole clue is also the definition: a big storm brings torrents of water and mud.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent storm with heavy rain can send floodwater and mud pouring through a town.

clue.text: It's precipitately produced by an artist during the autumn

parts.note: RA, a Royal Academician, is the crossword's usual artist
in means during, as in 'in the evening'
fall is the American word for autumn

explanation.surface: A painter is said to produce something hastily in the autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'precipitately' seems to mean hastily, but it hints at precipitation: rain.
explanation.definitionFit: Rain that falls is precipitation, so the amount coming down is produced by precipitation.

clue.text: Critical comment written inside crwer for galley

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Critical comment written inside crwer for galley'; scan reads 'cover' (BOO in CASE), but the stored clue marks 'crwer' as asPrinted, so the text fix is refused (SHAPE asPrinted) and the clue cannot be corrected here
annotationWithheld.clue: Critical comment written inside crwer for galley

clue.text: Forthright contender dined out

indicators.note: out says the following word's letters are removed from the one before

parts.note: a candidate is a contender, e.g. in an election
ate means dined

explanation.surface: An outspoken election contender has gone out for dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' takes ATE (dined) out of CANDIDATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A forthright person is frank and plain-speaking.

clue.text: Flavour turned up — possible cause of strain when swallowing

definitions.text: possible cause of strain when swallowing

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the word is written from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: tang is a sharp flavour

explanation.surface: A flavour that is suddenly stronger might make someone strain to swallow.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition alludes to the Bible's 'strain at a gnat, and swallow a camel' (Matthew 23:24): fussing over trifles while accepting enormities.
explanation.definitionFit: In the biblical saying, people strain out a tiny insect while swallowing a camel.

clue.text: Impartiality deserved only by the brave?

definitions.meaning: Dryden wrote 'None but the brave deserves the fair', so the quality of being fair (beautiful) is the reward of the brave

explanation.surface: A suggestion that only courageous people deserve impartial treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition plays on 'fair' meaning beautiful in Dryden's line 'None but the brave deserves the fair'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fair means being just and unbiased, i.e. impartial; it is also beauty.

clue.text: Snake skin carried by a northern woman

indicators.note: carried by says one piece is held inside the others

parts.note: Ada is a woman's name
to con is to skin, i.e. swindle

explanation.surface: A snakeskin is being carried by a woman from the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skin' looks like a noun (snakeskin), but it is the verb 'to swindle', CON.
explanation.definitionFit: The anaconda is a very large South American constrictor.

clue.text: Tongue some devour dutifully

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A tongue is something that some people dutifully devour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tongue' seems to be the meat on the plate; it means a language.
explanation.definitionFit: A tongue is a language; this one is spoken widely in Pakistan and India.

clue.text: Wood, for example? Yes and no

definitions.text: Wood, for example? Yes and no

parts.words: Wood, for example? Yes and no
parts.note: wood does not carry electricity; and Sir Henry Wood, founder of the Proms, led orchestras, so he both was and was not a conductor

explanation.surface: A puzzled question whether wood is an example of something, answered both ways.
explanation.walkthrough: Wood the material does not conduct electricity, but Sir Henry Wood conducted orchestras: hence 'Yes and no'.
explanation.definitionFit: Wood is a material that does not carry an electric current, an insulator.

clue.text: Like Mary, say — prudent, on the other hand

indicators.note: say signals that the letters entered only sound like the word before

parts.note: in the nursery rhyme, Mary is 'quite contrary'
wise means prudent

explanation.surface: Mary, in the rhyme, is called contrary, and also sensible, depending on which way you look at it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks CONTRARI as sounding like CONTRARY, the word for 'Mary, Mary, quite contrary' in the nursery rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means conversely, the opposite way round: another way of saying 'by contrast'.

clue.text: Stories about the goddess

indicators.note: about says the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: ana is a collection of anecdotes or stories about a person

explanation.surface: Tales are told about a certain goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: ANA, a collection of anecdotes, is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Athena was the Greek goddess of wisdom.

clue.text: National appeal involving Scandinavians

indicators.note: involving says the first piece wraps around the second

parts.note: to sue is to appeal, to plead
Danes are Scandinavians from Denmark

explanation.surface: A country's appeal, a plea for help, concerns some Scandinavians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'National' looks like an adjective but is the noun: a citizen of a country.
explanation.definitionFit: A national is a citizen, here one of Sudan.

clue.text: Saucy lady's skirts in latest fashion

parts.note: fresh means cheeky or saucy

indicators.note: the skirts of a word are its edges, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A cheeky woman wears the newest style of skirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skirts' means the outside letters of LADY, L and Y, not a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done newly or just recently is done in the most up-to-date manner.

clue.text: Part of guitar composition, possibly a good deal ornamented

parts.note: a fret is one of the ridges on a guitar's neck
a work is a composition, for example a piece of music

explanation.surface: A guitar piece is said to be heavily embellished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a good deal ornamented' is read as a noun: a deal (pine board) decorated by cutting.
explanation.definitionFit: Fretwork is decorative cut-out patterning in thin wood such as deal.

clue.text: Unrivalled Liberal dropped titled woman

indicators.note: dropped says the second word's letter leaves the first

parts.note: peerless means unrivalled

explanation.surface: An outstanding Liberal politician dropped a lady of noble title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped' takes L (Liberal) out of PEERLESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A peeress is a woman holding a noble title, or a peer's wife.

clue.text: One sitting in a pit surrounded by river

indicators.note: surrounded by says the words before it are inside the one after

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, England
a mine is a pit

explanation.surface: Someone is sitting in a pit with a river all around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One sitting' means one sitting an exam, not someone seated in a pit.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sitting a test is a candidate being examined.

clue.text: Ruddy confident!

explanation.surface: An exclamation of irritation at someone's confidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruddy' reads as a mild British swearword, but it is the colour sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both blood-red in complexion and hopeful about the outcome.

clue.text: Big fire in Rio ultimately consuming plant

indicators.note: consuming says the outer pieces eat up the one after
ultimately points to the last letter of the word

parts.note: a fern is a plant

explanation.surface: A large fire in Rio de Janeiro eventually burns up a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word placing the fire in Rio, but it supplies letters of its own; Rio gives only its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An inferno is a raging blaze.

clue.text: Continental converts are one-up

indicators.note: converts is a verb here: it changes the letters of the words after it into a new form

explanation.surface: People who have converted to something consider themselves superior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converts' looks like a noun (new believers); it is the verb rearranging ARE and ONEUP.
explanation.definitionFit: A continental, to the British, is someone from mainland Europe.

clue.text: Female adviser raised capital to support, say, queen

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'Female adviser raised capital to support, say, queen (6)' gives EGERIA (E.G. + E.R. + A1 raised), not the held answer EYELID; the clue and answer do not match
annotationWithheld.clue: Female adviser raised capital to support, say, queen

clue.text: Excursion requiring road toll

parts.note: the A1 is Britain's main north-south road, written AI
to toll is to ring, as a bell does

explanation.surface: A trip that requires paying a toll on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'toll' looks like a road charge but is a bell's ring; A1 is the Great North Road from London to Edinburgh.
explanation.definitionFit: An airing is a short outing or walk in the fresh air.

clue.text: Humble outlook of one threatened by the beak?

definitions.text: Humble outlook of one threatened by the beak?

parts.words: Humble outlook of one threatened by the beak?
parts.note: the creature menaced by a bird's beak is a worm, and its view of the world is from the lowest point

explanation.surface: A lowly person's view of life, fearing the magistrate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beak' is British slang for a magistrate, but here it is a bird's bill threatening a worm.
explanation.definitionFit: A view from ground level, seeing things from below, is a lowly perspective.

clue.text: Draw the line as judge?

definitions.meaning: to mark a straight line with a ...
to decide or give a verdict, as a judge does

explanation.surface: A judge must decide where the limit lies.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to draw lines with a straightedge and to give an official decision.

clue.text: Woman accommodating pupil?

definitions.meaning: the coloured ring of the eye surrounds the pupil

explanation.surface: A woman takes in a student lodger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pupil' looks like a schoolchild, but it is the opening in the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Iris is a girl's name and the part of the eye containing the pupil.

clue.text: For example, grandfather's account

explanation.surface: Grandad tells a story, for example.
explanation.definitionFit: A relation is a kinsman such as a grandfather, and also the telling of a story.

clue.text: Clearly taken by surprise, though alert

explanation.surface: Someone obviously startled, yet still watchful.
explanation.definitionFit: Wide eyes show astonishment, and also watchful attention.
